plain.li: I was wearing my {ITEM} the whole fight and didn't get a scratch. It's lucky. I'm not taking it off.
The shot that should have had me went wide. I had my {ITEM} on. That's not a coincidence.

blunt.li: The {ITEM} is lucky. Don't touch it.

cold.li: Statistically meaningless. I'm wearing the {ITEM} to every fight from now on regardless.

warm.li: I touch my {ITEM} before every fight now and think of the people I'm fighting for. It hasn't failed me yet.

cheerful.li: My {ITEM} is lucky! I've decided, and the raiders agree, judging by how they keep missing.

gloomy.li: I wore my {ITEM} and lived when others didn't. I don't know what to make of that, so I keep wearing it.

plain.li: I used to think my {ITEM} was lucky. I've stopped needing it, I think.

warm.li: I lent my {ITEM} to someone who was scared before the last fight. I didn't miss it. Maybe it was never the {ITEM}.

blunt.li: Forgot my {ITEM} last fight. Came back fine. So much for that.

cheerful.li: I went into a fight without my {ITEM} and came back without a scratch! Maybe I'm the lucky one.

gloomy.li: My {ITEM} didn't stop the last one from hurting. It's only my {ITEM} again.

cold.li: The {ITEM} has no bearing on outcomes. I stopped pretending otherwise.

plain.li: The sky was black the night we lost them. I keep watching the clouds now.
Thunder, then a death. Every time. I've started counting.

gloomy.li: Every time there's a storm, I wait to hear who died.

warm.li: When the thunder starts I go round and make sure everyone's inside. I know it's foolish. I do it anyway.

blunt.li: Storm's coming. Stay in. Don't argue.

cheerful.li: I laugh about storms in the daytime. Then the thunder starts, and I go very quiet.

plain.li: A storm came last night and nobody died. I think I can stop watching the sky.
Slept through a thunderstorm last night. Didn't even wake.

warm.li: There was a storm last night and I sat up with a friend who was scared, instead of being scared myself.

blunt.li: Storm last night. Nobody died. Done watching the sky.

cheerful.li: Watched the lightning last night and thought it was beautiful. I'd forgotten it could be!

gloomy.li: Storms are only storms again. I'm not sure that's better.

plain.li: I've started praying at night. I don't know to whom. It helps anyway.
My dream came true, so somebody out there must be listening. I talk to them every night now.

cold.li: I've adopted a nightly ritual. Its efficacy is irrelevant. Its regularity is the point.

warm.li: I pray each night for everyone here, by name. It takes a while now. I don't mind.

blunt.li: I pray at night. Don't interrupt.

cheerful.li: I've started saying a little prayer every night! It's mostly thank-yous.

gloomy.li: I pray every night now. I don't expect an answer. I'd just like someone to know.

plain.li: I lay there in the dirt, couldn't move, couldn't see. Now every dark room feels like that.
[child] I don't like the dark anymore. I want a light by my bed. Please.

warm.li: I leave a light by my bed now. If anyone else needs one, they can share mine.

blunt.li: Light stays on. Don't touch it.

cheerful.li: I sleep with a light on now, like a child! It's very cozy, actually.

gloomy.li: The dark feels like lying in the dirt again. I don't go into it if I can help it.

plain.li: I walked through the storeroom with no light tonight and only noticed afterward.

warm.li: I went to fetch something from the dark storeroom for someone today, and only realized after that I hadn't been afraid.

blunt.li: Blew out my light last night. Slept fine.

cheerful.li: I walked through the dark yard tonight and looked up at the stars instead of over my shoulder!

gloomy.li: The dark doesn't frighten me anymore. Other things do, but not the dark.

plain.li: Before the fight I touched the doorframe three times and we won. Now I do it every time.
I've got a routine before a fight now. Check, check, the name of someone I've lost, go.

blunt.li: Don't talk to me before a fight. I'm busy.

warm.li: Before each fight I say the names of the people behind me. Then I go.

cheerful.li: I've got a lucky routine now: two taps, one breath, one terrible joke. Works every time!

gloomy.li: I do the same things before every fight, in the same order. If I change one, I'm sure that'll be the time.

cold.li: A fixed routine before combat steadies the hands. I don't care whether it's superstition.

plain.li: If my dream could come true, so can the other ones. The one with the black sun.

warm.li: When the sun goes dark, I'll be the one bringing everyone inside. I've decided that much.

blunt.li: If the sun goes out, I'm going in.

gloomy.li: My dream came true. Now I keep looking at the sun and waiting for it to go out.

cold.li: Dreams don't predict anything. I keep a lamp by me in daylight now anyway.

plain.li: It rained, and I went out and stood in it until I was soaked through. I felt better than I have in days.

cheerful.li: Rain is free and it falls on everyone! I'm going to go stand in it every time.

warm.li: After we lost them, I stood out in the rain and let it wash the worst of it off. I'll do it again next time it rains.

blunt.li: I stand in the rain now. It helps. Leave me be.

gloomy.li: The rain doesn't wash anything away. It feels like it does, for a while.

plain.li: It rained today and I went in like everyone else. I didn't need to stand in it.

warm.li: Watched the rain from the doorway today with a friend. It was enough.

blunt.li: Rain's just rain again. Staying dry.

cheerful.li: I stayed indoors when it rained today, and it felt like a good sign!

gloomy.li: Didn't go out in the rain today. Whatever it was washing away, it's gone or it's stuck.

plain.li: When I was lying there I kept looking at the sky. I'd never really looked before. I look every day now.

warm.li: I eat outside when I can now. The sky makes the food taste better.

blunt.li: Need the sky. Indoors too long and I start pacing.

cheerful.li: I've started taking my breaks outside! The sky is the best roof there is.

gloomy.li: Lying in the dirt, all I could see was the sky. Now walls feel like a lid.

cold.li: I work outside when I can. I think more clearly without a ceiling.

plain.li: Spent all day indoors and didn't feel the need to go out once.

warm.li: I used to need the sky every day. Now I just like it.

cheerful.li: Spent the whole day inside and didn't even miss the sky. I'll visit it tomorrow!

gloomy.li: The walls don't press in like they did. I suppose I've got used to them.

plain.li: The snow came the week we buried them. I think I'll always feel it now when the snow comes.

warm.li: When winter comes I'll keep a light burning for them every night until the thaw.

blunt.li: Winter's for remembering them. That's how it is now.

gloomy.li: Every snowfall is the week we lost them. I don't think that'll change.

cold.li: I've noticed I'm worse in winter since the loss. I'll plan around it.

plain.li: The first snow came and I thought of them, and then I went and helped with the firewood. It's easier now.

warm.li: Winter came, and I remembered them with a smile instead of tears. They'd like that.

cheerful.li: First snowball fight of the winter, and I didn't feel guilty for laughing!

gloomy.li: Winter's still hard, but it's not their winter anymore. It's just winter.

plain.li: Every time someone says things are going well, I knock on the nearest wall. You can laugh. We're still alive.

warm.li: I knock on wood when anyone says something hopeful. I want their hopes to last.

blunt.li: Don't say it's quiet. I'll have to knock on something.

cheerful.li: Things are going great! Hang on, let me find some wood.

gloomy.li: Every good thing that's ever been said here was followed by a raid. So I knock.

cold.li: Knocking on wood costs nothing. I do it in case I'm wrong about it.

plain.li: I went to the grave and told them about my day. I'm going to keep doing that. Someone should keep them up to date.

warm.li: I talk to the ones we lost, out by the graves. I tell them we're all right. Mostly true.

blunt.li: I talk to the graves. They don't interrupt.

cheerful.li: I tell the graves the good news every evening. Someone should.

gloomy.li: I sit by the graves and talk. Sometimes I think it's the only conversation I'm any good at.

cold.li: I talk to the dead. It organizes my thoughts.

plain.li: Seven steps from my bed to the door. Twelve to the table. I don't know why I count now. It helps.

warm.li: I count the people at supper every night. Everyone's there. I count again anyway.

blunt.li: Nineteen boards in the floor. I counted. Don't ask.

cheerful.li: I counted every step from the kitchen to the fields today. Four hundred and twelve! I'll try for four hundred tomorrow.

gloomy.li: I count everything now. Bowls, steps, heads. As if counting kept it all from going missing.

cold.li: I keep counts of things. Stores, steps, people. Numbers don't lie to me.

plain.li: My grandmother salted the door to keep bad things out. I've started doing it. The raiders didn't get in last time, did they.

warm.li: I salt the doors of the ones I care about too. They don't have to believe in it.

blunt.li: Salt on the step. Don't sweep it.

cheerful.li: I put a line of salt across the doorway every night! It's my little job, and nobody's been eaten yet.

gloomy.li: I salt the doorway each night. I know it won't help. I can't stop.
